customers.description: One row per registered customer/account. Used for questions about who bought things, customer segments, or geography.

columns.customer_id: Unique identifier for a customer. Join key to orders.customer_id.
columns.email: Customer's contact email, unique per customer.
columns.signup_date: Date (YYYY-MM-DD) the customer created their account.
columns.segment: Business segment the customer belongs to: 'retail' (individual buyers) or 'enterprise' (business accounts). 'Key accounts' or 'VIP' in business speak usually means segment = 'enterprise'.

business_rules: 'New customers' typically means signup_date within the last 90 days relative to the latest order_date in the data.
'Enterprise customers' and 'key accounts' both map to segment = 'enterprise'.

products.description: Product catalog. Used for questions about pricing, categories, or inventory/stock levels.

columns.product_id: Unique identifier for a product. Join key to order_items.product_id.
columns.category: Product category, e.g. Electronics, Furniture, Stationery.
columns.unit_price: Current list price per unit, in USD.
columns.in_stock: Units currently available in inventory. 'Out of stock' means in_stock = 0; 'low stock' means in_stock < 30.

business_rules: 'Best sellers' means highest total quantity sold via order_items, not highest unit_price.

orders.description: One row per customer order (a shopping cart checkout event). Used for questions about revenue, order counts, order status, or trends over time.

columns.order_id: Unique identifier for an order. Join key to order_items.order_id.
columns.customer_id: The customer who placed the order. Foreign key to customers.customer_id.

business_rules: 'Revenue' and 'sales' should only include orders with status = 'completed' unless the question explicitly asks about pending or cancelled orders too.
'Order value' or 'order total' = SUM(order_items.quantity * order_items.unit_price) for that order_id.

order_items.description: Line items within an order — one row per distinct product within an order, with the quantity and price paid at that time. This is the primary table for revenue and quantity calculations.

columns.order_item_id: Unique identifier for the line item.
columns.order_id: The order this line item belongs to. Foreign key to orders.order_id.
columns.product_id: The product purchased in this line item. Foreign key to products.product_id.
columns.quantity: Number of units of the product purchased in this line item.
columns.unit_price: Price per unit at the time of purchase (may differ from the product's current unit_price).

business_rules: Always use order_items.unit_price (price paid at purchase time) for revenue calculations, not products.unit_price (current list price), unless the question is explicitly about current pricing.
